bug_semantics: Interpretation conflict between SandboxPolicy's security matcher and the executor's tokenizer (CWE-436): isCommandAllowed() evaluated the RAW command string (quotes preserved) against the blockedCommands/allowedCommands glob lists, while ShellExecutor.execute() ran the identical string through parseCommandLine()/tokenizeCommand(), which STRIP quotes and collapse whitespace before the spawn. A command like "git" status (quoted 'git') fails to match blocklist patterns such as git* on the raw string but tokenizes to the argv [git, status] that the executor runs — and likewise a quoted 'rm -rf /' style payload or an allowed-list command padded with quotes/irregular whitespace can slip past approval gates. The result: blocklist checks and approval gates are evaded while the executor runs the exact unquoted dangerous argv. At v5.15.0 this raw-vs-canonical split is verbatim in lib/agent-runtime.ts (parseCommandLine used only as a metachar gate; matchesAny still fed `trimmed`).
flaw_origin: Commit 379f77656b578144e03415c5b134d8309a4b5792 ("fix: v5.9.1 — GHSA-qw6v-5fcf-5666 shell command injection (CWE-78, Critical) + permission_denied audit logging", 2026-06-02, author/committer jovanSAPFIONEER <jovan@sapfioneer.example>, parent 7778eed65b5e628183a6091d74ce92de3407507c) first wrote the divergent-representation design the advisory names: it introduced parseCommandLine() — the quote-stripping/whitespace-collapsing tokenizer used by tokenizeCommand() for shell:false execution — while isCommandAllowed() KEPT matching security patterns against the raw trimmed string (matchesAny(trimmed, ...) at the fixed-up lines 343/349 of the post-commit file). The executor/tokenizer (quote-stripping semantics) and the matcher (raw-string semantics) were born in this same commit with the interpretation conflict already present; the executor itself (spawn with /bin/sh -c) predates it at 58ebcf3a491efd4358a47d317afbf9f6deca5002 (Phase 9, 2026-04-02), but that executor matched and ran the SAME raw string, so no representation divergence existed before 379f7765 — the advisory's flaw (matcher evaluates quotes-preserved input, executor consumes quotes-stripped argv) begins exactly with this commit's split into two representations.

evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-73615 / GHSA-9v4f-j8cv-fhxw): Network-AI before 5.15.1 — SandboxPolicy evaluates raw command strings with quotes preserved while the executor tokenizes by stripping quotes before execution; attackers craft quoted commands that evade blocklist checks and approval gates while the executor runs the identical unquoted dangerous argv (CWE-436).

BIC introduction: `git show 379f7765 -- lib/agent-runtime.ts` — adds SHELL_METACHARACTERS set, parseCommandLine() (quote-stripping tokenizer: `if (quote) { if (ch === quote) quote = null; else current += ch; ... }`), gates isCommandAllowed() on parsed flags, adds tokenizeCommand() returning stripped argv, and rewrites ShellExecutor.spawnCommand from `spawn('/bin/sh', ['-c', command])` to `shell: false` execution of `this.policy.tokenizeCommand(command)` argv. The matcher still matches the raw string: post-commit file /tmp/v591.ts shows :337 `const parsed = parseCommandLine(trimmed)` (metachar gate only), :343 `matchesAny(trimmed, this.config.blockedCommands)`, :349 `matchesAny(trimmed, this.config.allowedCommands)` — matcher on raw quotes-preserved string vs executor consuming quote-stripped argv: the advisory's divergence, complete in this commit.

Executor origin (pre-divergence context): 58ebcf3a491efd4358a47d317afbf9f6deca5002 (Phase 9, 2026-04-02, jovanSAPFIONEER) created SandboxPolicy + ShellExecutor; there the executor passed the raw command to `/bin/sh -c` (BIC dump :392-395) and the SAME raw string was matched — one representation, no conflict. Not the BIC for this advisory.

Vulnerable state at advisory floor: `git show v5.15.0:lib/agent-runtime.ts` (:337-356) — parseCommandLine used solely to reject unquoted metacharacters; blocklist/allowlist matched against `trimmed` with quotes intact; executor (tokenizeCommand) strips quotes and collapses whitespace. Single quotes, double quotes, or extra whitespace thus alter matcher input without altering executed argv (e.g. blocklist `rm *` vs input `'rm -rf /'`).

Fix: f294d33642a9c5218f1a64d7b159ca70d06f63e4 (2026-07-28, jovanSAPFIONEER, "Security: fix GHSA-743h-jr5x-mpcr ... and GHSA-9v4f-j8cv-fhxw (SandboxPolicy quote/whitespace matcher bypass); bump to v5.15.1") — adds private canonicalize() (parseCommandLine then argv.join(' ')) and switches blocklist/allowlist to matchesAny(canonical, ...) with the comment 'Matching the raw string here let quoting or extra whitespace evade both the blocklist and the allowlist while the tokenized executor ran the identical unquoted command (GHSA-9v4f-j8cv-fhxw)'. `git tag --contains f294d336` → v5.15.1 (first fixed tag; advisory 'before 5.15.1' consistent). fix_sha = direct_fix_sha = f294d336 (single release commit; no separate backport branch).
Marker screening: NONE sentinels on 58ebcf3a, 379f7765, b7be8c6f, f294d336 — all human jovanSAPFIONEER; no AI/co-authored trailers anywhere on the flaw wave or the fix.
reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory names an interpretation conflict — SandboxPolicy matches raw (quotes-preserved) strings while the executor tokenizes (strips quotes) before running, letting quoted commands evade blocklist/approval gates. Code archaeology: the two representations were introduced TOGETHER by 379f7765 (2026-06-02): it created parseCommandLine/tokenizeCommand for shell:false execution while leaving isCommandAllowed matching the raw string — the divergence the advisory describes exists from this commit onward (verified verbatim at v5.15.0). The earlier 58ebcf3a executor matched and ran the same raw string, so no divergence existed there; 58ebcf3a is context, not BIC. BIC = 379f7765, single-commit flaw (squash_decomposed=false). Fix = f294d336 canonicalize() change, first in v5.15.1, matching the advisory floor. AI decision: BIC-only attribution — all flaw-wave and fix commits carry only the human identity jovanSAPFIONEER with no AI markers ('ClaudeHookBridge' in the fix message is a component name, not authorship), so NOT_AI.
